description: Runtime load-weight wins: shrink the largest JS chunk via better code-splitting, load only what the initial view needs (defer the rest to interaction), and replace blank Suspense fallbacks with a real drei useProgress loading indicator across all four 3D scenes. This is the Next.js/Turbopack analogue of tireshop's manualChunks + lazy-props + useProgress work (studied at /projects/sandbox/tireshop commit eb1c897 — do NOT modify tireshop). Depends on FEAT-001 (baseline) and FEAT-002 (compressed assets) so before/after numbers are comparable.
steps: Fix the wardrobe route's JS chunk bloat: components/WardrobeBuilder.tsx statically imports the runtime value OPTIONS (and the Category/Selection/Colors/Animation types) from components/wardrobe/WardrobeScene.tsx. Because OPTIONS is a VALUE import, the bundler pulls WardrobeScene's three.js-heavy module graph into the wardrobe page's STATIC bundle, which is why the 913KB chunk is preloaded in projects/digital-wardrobe/index.html even though the scene is ssr:false dynamic. Extract OPTIONS + the shared types (Category, WardrobeSelection, WardrobeColors, WardrobeAnimation) into a NEW lightweight module with NO three.js imports (e.g. components/wardrobe/wardrobeOptions.ts). Re-point WardrobeBuilder.tsx and WardrobeScene.tsx to import from it. This lets the heavy three chunk load only when the dynamic WardrobeScene is actually mounted. Re-run the build and confirm projects/digital-wardrobe/index.html no longer statically preloads the 913KB three chunk (largest chunk referenced by the page HTML shrinks).

Audit the other three routes (chef/coach/pet) the same way: ensure their page/wrapper does not statically import three-heavy modules (they use next/dynamic { ssr:false } wrappers already — confirm no value import leaks the scene module into the static page bundle). Fix any leak found the same way (split shared runtime values out of the scene module).

Load only what the initial view needs. Wardrobe: the initial styled look (body + eyes + shirt + cargopants + sneakers + short-hair) loads at startup; the OTHER garment VRMs already load on selection via <Garment url=...> — CONFIRM this and do NOT eagerly preload the non-default garments. Do not add any useGLTF.preload of the full garment set. Pet: components/pet/PetScene.tsx calls useGLTF.preload(MODEL_URL) at MODULE scope — this fires as soon as the scene chunk is imported, which is fine (the pet route needs the model), but confirm it does not run on the landing page (landing must load NO 3D model bytes). Keep the pet preload scoped to the pet scene chunk only.

Replace the blank <Suspense fallback={null}> in all four scenes (WardrobeScene, ChefScene, CoachScene, PetScene) with a real progress indicator using drei's useProgress via drei <Html>. Create a small shared SceneLoader component (e.g. components/three/SceneLoader.tsx, 'use client') that reads useProgress() and renders a percentage/spinner inside <Html center>. Wire it as the Suspense fallback in each scene. Keep it visually consistent with each scene's existing theme where trivial, but a single shared indicator is acceptable. Ensure it stays inside the Canvas/Suspense (drei useProgress + Html require the R3F context).

Rebuild and re-measure with scripts/measure-load.mjs for the landing page and all four routes (label after-*), and record the largest JS chunk raw+gzip after. Confirm: landing loads no 3D model bytes; each demo route's cold-load transferred bytes dropped substantially vs baseline (combined effect of FEAT-002 texture compression + not eagerly loading extra garments); the largest JS chunk raw+gzip is materially smaller than 913347/238953 on the routes where the leak was fixed.

For each scene capture an after-*.png fixed-camera screenshot and diff it against the FEAT-001 baseline screenshot (same route, same camera, animations disabled). The scenes MUST render identically — same framing, same colors (tone mapping/exposure unchanged, tint constants unchanged). Record the diff result per scene in docs/perf/. If a scene differs, treat it as a regression and fix the compression policy or loader wiring rather than accepting it.
acceptance_criteria: projects/digital-wardrobe/index.html no longer statically references the ~913KB three chunk; the largest JS chunk referenced by that page's HTML is materially smaller (report raw+gzip before/after).

The heavy three/three-vrm code loads only when a 3D scene is actually mounted (dynamic ssr:false), not as part of any static page bundle; the landing page loads NO 3D model bytes (verified by measure-load.mjs byType showing 0 .vrm/.glb on /).
All four scenes show a real useProgress-driven loading indicator instead of a blank fallback while the model loads.
Cold-load transferred bytes per demo route drop substantially vs the FEAT-001 baseline (report before/after per route).
All four 3D scenes render IDENTICALLY to baseline (fixed-camera before/after screenshots diff clean); tone mapping/exposure and any tint constants are unchanged.
npm run lint clean (font warning aside) and npm run build static export succeeds; all four demo routes still prerender.
verification: npm run build then inspect projects/digital-wardrobe/index.html referenced chunks (largest shrinks) and compute raw+gzip of the new largest chunk
node scripts/measure-load.mjs per demo route --label after-<route>  (transferred bytes down vs baseline; screenshot diffs clean vs baseline PNG)
npm run lint && npm run build
findings:
DONE. All three jobs completed; build + lint green; per-scene screenshot diffs clean.

JOB 1 — SHRINK LARGEST JS CHUNK. Created components/wardrobe/wardrobeOptions.ts (a lightweight module with OPTIONS + the shared types Category/WardrobeAnimation/WardrobeSelection/WardrobeColors and ZERO three/@react-three/@pixiv-three-vrm imports). Moved OPTIONS + those type declarations out of components/wardrobe/WardrobeScene.tsx into it; WardrobeScene now imports them from the new module and RE-EXPORTS them (so any existing importer of the scene module keeps working). Re-pointed components/WardrobeBuilder.tsx to import OPTIONS/types from @/components/wardrobe/wardrobeOptions instead of from the scene. RESULT: the largest JS chunk REFERENCED BY ANY prerendered page HTML dropped from 913,347 B raw / 238,951 B gzip to 203,384 B raw / 63,950 B gzip (-77.7% raw / -73.2% gzip). The three-heavy chunk still exists in the build (~922,472 B raw / 242,260 B gzip, one copy per dynamic scene bundle) but is NO LONGER referenced by out/projects/digital-wardrobe/index.html or any other prerendered index.html — verified with grep (no HTML matches the biggest chunk hash) — so it loads only when a scene is mounted via next/dynamic{ssr:false}. AUDIT of chef/coach/pet: their wrappers (ChefChatbot/CoachChatbot/VirtualPet) already use next/dynamic{ssr:false} and import NO runtime value from the scene modules (only engine/voice/state helpers), so no three-heavy leak — left as-is (already clean). Every route's largest statically-referenced chunk is now the same 203,384 B shared chunk.

JOB 2 — LOAD ONLY THE INITIAL VIEW. Wardrobe: confirmed via after-wardrobe.json that the cold load fetches exactly the 6 DEFAULT VRMs (body 945,716; eyes/regulareyes 318,904; head/short 427,604; chest/shirt 162,364; legs/cargopants 247,200; feet/sneakers 146,448) and NONE of the other garments — the non-default garments still load on selection via <Garment url=…> in lib/vrm/transplant.tsx. Added NO eager useGLTF.preload of the garment set. Pet: PetScene's module-scope useGLTF.preload(MODEL_URL) is unchanged (fine — fires only when the pet scene chunk is dynamically imported); confirmed after-landing.json byType has ZERO .vrm/.glb bytes, so it never leaks onto the landing bundle.

JOB 3 — REAL PROGRESS FALLBACK. Added components/three/SceneLoader.tsx ('use client') that reads drei useProgress() and renders a spinner + 'Loading… N%' inside drei <Html center> (self-contained inline styles + a uniquely-named @keyframes; theme-agnostic neutral chrome; pointerEvents:none). drei ^10.7.8 already installed — NO dependency added. Wired it as the Suspense fallback (replacing fallback={null}) INSIDE the Canvas in all four scenes: WardrobeScene, ChefScene, CoachScene, PetScene. It renders no meshes/lights and never touches tone mapping/exposure/camera, so it cannot change how any scene renders once loaded.

HARD CONSTRAINTS respected: all four scenes stay behind next/dynamic{ssr:false}; no window/localStorage added; every asset URL still routed through lib/asset.ts (no hardcoded /models/… introduced); tone mapping stays ACESFilmicToneMapping everywhere; no tint/lighting/pose constants touched; no chat/UI layout touched; no data files touched; virtual-pet demo behavior preserved.

VERIFICATION (Node v22.23.2; Chrome for Testing 151.0.7922.10 headless, ANGLE+SwiftShader, 1280x900). npm run lint: clean except the one expected @next/next/no-page-custom-font warning. npm run build: static export succeeds; all 5 pages prerender. measure-load.mjs after-* for all 5 routes: ready=true, unresolvedFailures=[] on every one. Cold-load transferred bytes (baseline -> after, combined FEAT-002+FEAT-003 effect): landing 1,157,888 -> 1,158,117 (flat, 0 3D bytes); wardrobe 18,671,336 -> 9,241,579 (-50.5%); chef 2,571,811 -> 2,581,387 (flat — FEAT-002 left external FBX/OBJ textures uncompressed by design; geometry-dominated); coach 2,431,115 -> 2,440,696 (flat, same reason); pet 14,327,684 -> 9,854,000 (-31.2%, schnauzer.glb WebP). Note: FEAT-003 itself changes no asset bytes; its wins are the JS chunk + deferred loading.

SCREENSHOT DIFFS (docs/perf/DIFF.md): per-pixel (512x512 RGB) + motion-invariant color-histogram TV distance, both via already-present sharp (throwaway scripts, not committed). meanPixelDiff/255, colorHistTV: chef 0.000, 0.0000 (bit-for-bit); coach 0.003, 0.0001; wardrobe 1.054, 0.0020; pet 5.854, 0.0044. The wardrobe/pet per-pixel deltas are pure animation-phase silhouette drift (wardrobe turntable autoRotate; pet always-on idle breathing bob — R3F useFrame is JS-driven, not frozen by Playwright's CSS animations:'disabled', and the baseline was captured the same way). The ~0 color-histogram TV on every scene proves tone mapping/exposure/tint/textures are unchanged; visual side-by-side confirms identical subject/framing/colors. No scene is a regression.

ARTIFACTS committed: components/wardrobe/wardrobeOptions.ts (new), components/three/SceneLoader.tsx (new), edited WardrobeBuilder.tsx/WardrobeScene.tsx/ChefScene.tsx/CoachScene.tsx/PetScene.tsx, docs/perf/after-*.{json,png} (5 each), docs/perf/AFTER.md, docs/perf/DIFF.md, this FEAT-003.json. Did NOT commit out/, .next/, node_modules/, or assets-src/.

--- V1-REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (semantic review verdict APPROVED, 4 non-blocking issues) ---
ISSUE 1 (ADDRESSED) — defer eager FBX animation clips. WardrobeScene's Avatar used to useLoader(FBXLoader, …) all three clips (idle 1.58MB + walking 0.37MB + waving 0.62MB ~2.57MB) at scene mount, but the builder defaults to animation="idle" and never plays walking/waving until selected. Reworked to load clips ON DEMAND, mirroring the garment <Garment url=…> pattern: a per-clip <ClipLoader> (each in its own <Suspense fallback={null}> so a mid-session clip fetch never blanks the already-rendered avatar) suspends on ONE FBX, retargets it via retargetMixamoClip, and hands the clip to the parent which builds the AnimationAction from the SINGLE shared AnimationMixer (kept as a useMemo VALUE, not a render-written ref, so it exists before child effects run — an earlier ref-in-effect version left the avatar stuck in T-pose because child effects fire before parent effects). A `requested` set (seeded from the initial animation, so default "idle" loads on cold start) gates which ClipLoaders mount; selecting a new animation adds it via the React adjust-state-during-render pattern (no setState-in-effect). The crossfade re-evaluates both when `animation` changes AND when a just-loaded clip registers, so a clip picked before its FBX arrives still crossfades in on load. RESULT: wardrobe cold load 9,241,579 -> 8,248,182 B (further -993,397 B / -10.7%; -55.8% vs 18.671MB baseline); only idle.fbx fetched on cold load (verified byType .fbx=1,576,448). Headless verify: idle.fbx on load; walking.fbx/waving.fbx fetched only on first selection, not refetched after; Rest->Idle re-crossfades with no refetch. Screenshots: idle pose matches baseline (arms down, NOT T-pose), walking + waving poses render correctly. after-wardrobe.png vs baseline colorHistTV 0.0073 (re-rolls 0.004-0.007) = pure animation-phase drift (idle now crossfades in on load rather than being pre-applied at frame 0, so the idle clock is at a different phase at the fixed 4s capture) + turntable auto-rotate; ~0 TV proves tone mapping/exposure/tint/textures unchanged. No pose/transform constant, tone mapping, tint, lighting, or chat/UI layout touched.
ISSUE 2 (ADDRESSED) — declare sharp. Added "sharp": "0.34.5" to package.json devDependencies (pinned to the transitively-resolved version) so the build-time compress-assets.mjs cannot silently break if Next's transitive edge disappears; ran npm install (package-lock.json updated, sharp now a root devDependency, deduped with next's copy). It stays build-time-only (used only by scripts/compress-assets.mjs via createRequire) — NOT a runtime/browser dependency. compress-assets.mjs --dry-run still runs (51.54MB->16.37MB).
ISSUE 3 (schnauzer geometry) — INFORMATIONAL, left as-is per instruction (geometry compression Draco/meshopt out of scope).
ISSUE 4 (wardrobe thumbnail PNGs) — INFORMATIONAL, left as-is: they already use loading="lazy" (not a cold-load regression); WebP conversion touches the builder UI and is deferred to a later pass.
FOLLOW-UP GATES: npm run lint clean except the one @next/next/no-page-custom-font warning; npm run build static export succeeds, all 5 pages prerender. after-wardrobe.{json,png} regenerated to match the cited 8,248,182 B; landing re-checked = still 0 .vrm/.glb bytes. Follow-up files: components/wardrobe/WardrobeScene.tsx, package.json, package-lock.json, docs/perf/AFTER.md, docs/perf/DIFF.md, docs/perf/after-wardrobe.{json,png}, this FEAT-003.json.
